hypothesis: A generic duel shield can exploit a repeatedly inferred high-power shooter by stopping, stepping laterally after a shot, and firing a low-power bullet across the inferred headon ray before the incoming bullet reaches the robot.
changes: Keep movement and gun data managers executing every tick; apply a round-local body override after normal movement and a shield-only branch before normal duel aiming.

Activate only in a battle that began as a duel, with own energy above35, fresh scan, current range at least275, and a true unprocessed firing wave age0..4, power at least2.4, and shot range at least275.
Require a new true wave whose fire time follows at least3 stationary ticks, target velocity below.01, and age at most6; deduplicate by fireTime.
Step alternating8pixels along the current body heading at maximum velocity2, with a prospective lateral offset at least4pixels from the old target ray and battlefield margin20.
After settling, reconstruct incoming direction from observed wave source to old stationary target, solve a continuous intercept, and plan firing for the next tick from the unchanged actual position.

Use power.1 first; only near a tick-boundary intercept consider powers.11.. .5 to improve the temporal phase margin. Require intercept distance at least60 and interception more than one full incoming tick before robot-box entry.

Fire only on the exact planned tick with cold gun, matching heading within1e-9 radians, matching position within1e-6pixels, and zero velocity; preserve logged projectile, shadow, and gun-wave tracking with actual bullet power.

Abort permanently for the round after3 received hits while active; return to ordinary movement and gun. Exit for the endgame when opponent energy is at most.2 and all true incoming waves have cleared the body.
Track actual shield bullets separately; print one TITAN_SHIELD line per round with active_ticks, attempts, shots, confirmed collisions, received hits, and aborted. No battle-memory format changes.

legality.sources: Public scans, own robot state and commands, existing energy-inferred movement waves, and public bullet events only. The incoming heading is a generic stationary-headon hypothesis, not an observed hidden bullet heading.

engine_conventions.incoming_wave_fire_time: MoveDataManager sets fireTime=scanTime-1, source=enemy state(scanTime-1), target=own state(scanTime-2).
engine_conventions.planning_elapsed: When planning at local timeT for local firing atT+1, incoming elapsed=T+1-wave.fireTime; own outgoing distance is0at local fire time.
engine_conventions.order: Load and fire with current heading/position, update bullet segments, then cool/turn/move robots and scan.
engine_conventions.bullet_collision: Exact nonparallel zero-width segment intersection. Collinear overlap is not a valid shield. Robot-box collision is checked before bullet collision in the same tick.

confirmation_order: Fresh original opponent C10screen; advance only with at least9wins, scorelead, and confirmed shield-specific bullet collisions.
Fresh original opponent C50only if C10qualifies; stop for review if C10orC50fails.
Fresh opponent D50only if C50qualifies, with the identical frozen source hash.
limitations: Shield accuracy depends on the observed shooter's future shots following the stationary-headon ray. Waves contain no exact hidden incoming heading.
Compile and production-method geometry checks cannot establish battle performance. The C10screen is a required feasibility measurement.
